newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas firms across curve, busiest in October.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas firms across curve, busiest in October.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract saw a healthy volume of trade done in October on Thursday afternoon at firmer levels, while prices for all months rose as liquidity improved in the afternoon session.

October saw 75 lots traded in only two transactions shortly before the close. One broker suggested a player was shorting October, feeling that it was overvalued. On Wednesday evening October had settled at 12.10 pence a therm, nearly 2.0 pence above the September settlement price and described by a broker as "way too high."
This differential led some to see October as due to find a new level nearer to the September price.

The front months continued to rise following the increases seen on Wednesday. The first four months from May to August traded for the last time at close to parity, with July at 10.225 pence slightly higher than the others which traded at 10.20 pence.

A total of 125 lots were done in 11 separate deals, with all the traded months seeing increases. Only 10 of these lots were done in the two-hour morning session. And there was reasonable depth to bids and offers in all periods, and in reasonably tight ranges, a broker said.
